title: Radioactive decay: types and properties; Fundamental interactions and exchange particles; Particles, antiparticles and classification; Photons and the photoelectric effect
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: P02-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; P02-2#t2 term and clue written for the game; P02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; P01-uk1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: N02-uk2#N.4, Q01-1#N.4c, Q01-1#N.9a, Q01-1#N.13.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Electromagnetic interaction
items.clue: Acts on charged particles only; infinite range.

items.label: Flavour
items.clue: Name for the type of a quark, such as up or down.

items.label: Weak interaction
items.clue: Acts on all quarks and all leptons; range about 10⁻¹⁸ m.

items.label: Meson
items.clue: Particle made of a quark and an antiquark, such as a pion.

questions.stem: The chart shows neutron number N against proton number Z. Starting from the nucleus marked with a dot, four arrows (one of them a loop back to the same nucleus) are meant to show the change produced by each of the four types of decay, as labelled. One of the four is drawn incorrectly. Which one?
A laser pointer emits light of wavelength 633 nm with a power of 5.0 mW. How many photons does it emit each second? Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
Predict first. Which observation from photoelectric experiments cannot be explained by the classical wave theory of light?

options.text: Photoelectrons are emitted without any measurable delay, even in very dim light.
More photoelectrons are emitted each second when the light is made much more intense.
More photoelectrons are emitted each second when the frequency of the light is raised.
Every photoelectron leaves the metal with kinetic energy exactly hf minus the work function.

questions.stem: Light whose photons each have energy 4.0 eV shines on three metals: X, with work function 2.0 eV; Y, with work function 3.0 eV; and Z, with work function 4.5 eV. Which statement about the maximum kinetic energy of the electrons emitted from each metal is correct?

options.text: Z's electrons have the greatest maximum kinetic energy, and X's electrons the least
X's electrons have the greatest maximum kinetic energy, and Z emits no electrons
All three metals emit electrons, each with the same maximum kinetic energy
Their maximum kinetic energies cannot be ranked without the light's intensity
